summary: Modern data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML directly where data lives, eliminating costly data movement by offering in-database model training, LLM inference via SQL functions, and vector similarity search for RAG and semantic applications. Native vector search is now common in cloud-native platforms (Snowflake, Databricks, MongoDB Atlas), while traditional relational engines like PostgreSQL, Aurora, and Redshift rely on extensions such as pgvector. The vector database market is projected to reach ~$17.91 billion by 2034 (24% CAGR), with roughly 75% of enterprise AI applications expected to depend on vector search by 2026.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless, SQL-accessible AI functions including hosted LLMs (via COMPLETE), task-specific functions (SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), Cortex Search for retrieval, and Cortex Analyst for natural-language querying. Also extended to Snowflake Postgres so developers can call Cortex functions from a managed Postgres environment.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with built-in vector similarity functions (VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE, VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.) and Cortex Search as a managed hybrid search service.
databases.llm_integration: Built-in hosted LLMs (e.g., Llama, Mistral, Claude, Snowflake Arctic) callable directly via Cortex SQL/Python functions; no external API wiring needed.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits per token/compute for Cortex functions; standard warehouse compute and storage charges apply separately.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization) using standard SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI for access to foundation models (Gemini, PaLM) via ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and remote model endpoints.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides VECTOR_SEARCH function with vector indexes (IVF) and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING for embedding generation directly in SQL.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI; call Gemini and other foundation models for generation and embeddings via remote models and ML.GENERATE_TEXT.
databases.pricing_notes: On-demand pricing by bytes processed or capacity-based (slots) for queries; LLM/Vertex calls billed via Vertex AI model usage in addition to BigQuery compute.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search to PostgreSQL, while pgai (and pgvectorscale) adds helper functions to generate embeddings and call LLM providers (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) directly from SQL, enabling RAG workflows inside the database. Commonly combined with LangChain for application-layer orchestration.
databases.vector_search_notes: Via extension (native to the PostgreSQL ecosystem). pgvector is an open-source extension providing a vector type with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes; it is not part of core Postgres but is the de facto standard and widely bundled by managed providers.
databases.llm_integration: pgai enables in-database calls to external LLM/embedding APIs (OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama, etc.); orchestration frameworks like LangChain are widely used on top.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; costs are only the underlying Postgres hosting/compute plus any third-party LLM API usage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications via SQL by calling Amazon SageMaker endpoints, Amazon Bedrock foundation models, and Amazon Comprehend directly from Aurora MySQL/PostgreSQL queries, without building custom integration code.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Vector search on Aurora is provided only through the pgvector extension on Aurora PostgreSQL, which is a third-party extension rather than a native Aurora ML capability.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker endpoints invoked via SQL functions; Comprehend for NLP tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora instance/storage/IO billing applies; ML inference incurs separate SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend charges based on usage.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML lets analysts create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL CREATE MODEL statements, automatically leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. It supports in-database inference and integration with Bedrock foundation models for generative AI from SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native as a general-purpose vector index. Redshift added limited vector support and can store embeddings, but it lacks a mature built-in vector similarity search service comparable to dedicated vector databases; vector-heavy workloads typically use OpenSearch or pgvector elsewhere.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon SageMaker for model training/inference and Amazon Bedrock LLMs invoked via SQL for generative tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed via Redshift compute (RPU/node hours) and storage; model training/inference incurs additional SageMaker and Bedrock charges.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling—model serving, foundation model APIs, fine-tuning, agent framework, and MLflow-based lifecycle management—on the lakehouse. Databricks Vector Search provides a managed vector index integrated with Unity Catalog governance.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a fully managed, serverless native vector database that auto-syncs with Delta tables and supports hybrid search with governance via Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs provide access to open and proprietary LLMs, custom fine-tuning, and an agent/RAG framework natively on the platform.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs) for compute, model serving, and vector search; plus underlying cloud infrastructure costs.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search enables semantic and RAG applications by storing embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and querying them with approximate nearest-neighbor search using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, combinable with metadata filters and full-text search.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is built into the managed Atlas service, providing HNSW-based ANN indexing with the $vectorSearch operator and hybrid search; embeddings and operational data live together in the same documents.
databases.llm_integration: No bundled LLM; integrates easily with external providers (OpenAI, Hugging Face, Bedrock, Vertex) and frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex for embedding generation and RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas cluster pricing; dedicated Search Nodes can be provisioned separately for vector workloads, billed by node size/hours.
